audit.name: Written law

newNodes.distinctFrom: kin_council governs one band; seasonal gatherings bring many bands together for a few weeks.

newNodes.name: Compensation for injury
newNodes.emerged: pre-literate practice (ethnographic analogy: payments in livestock and valuables); first written ~2,100 BCE in the laws of Ur-Nammu (silver for injuries)
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: compensation is paid in the valuables that circulate as gifts. kin_council: elders fix the price and witness the settlement. Both far earlier than the first written schedule (~2,100 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: compensation is paid in the valuables that circulate as gifts. kin_council: elders fix the price and witness the settlement. Both far earlier than the first written schedule (~2,100 BCE).
newNodes.desc: A killing or injury is settled by a fixed payment from the offender's kin to the victim's, set by the elders, instead of by revenge.
newNodes.effectRationale: A settled price ends the wrong; the feud that would have festered does not start.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customary_sanctions punish a band member; compensation settles wrongs between kin groups by payment.

newNodes.name: Witnessed agreements
newNodes.emerged: pre-literate practice; witness lists on Sumerian land-sale contracts by ~2,600 BCE (Fara)
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: obligations between partners precede formal agreements. token_counting: counted tokens record the quantities promised (~8,000 BCE). Both precede the first written witness lists (~2,600 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: obligations between partners precede formal agreements. token_counting: counted tokens record the quantities promised (~8,000 BCE). Both precede the first written witness lists (~2,600 BCE).
newNodes.desc: A sale, loan or pledge is made before named witnesses who can later swear to its terms, so a deal with a stranger can be enforced.
newNodes.effectRationale: Enforceable deals with strangers let goods move between villages where prices differ.
newNodes.distinctFrom: gift_exchange is reciprocity between partners; witnessed agreements bind strangers to stated terms.

newNodes.name: Household fields
newNodes.emerged: ~3,700 BCE Ceide Fields (Ireland), a stone-walled field system of separate holdings
newNodes.prereqRationale: cereal_cultivation: fields worth holding exist only once crops are sown (~11,500 BCE). kin_council: the household heads recognize each other's holdings.
newNodes.rationale: cereal_cultivation: fields worth holding exist only once crops are sown (~11,500 BCE). kin_council: the household heads recognize each other's holdings.
newNodes.desc: Each household works its own fields within marked boundaries and passes them to its heirs; the village recognizes the holding.
newNodes.effectRationale: A household that keeps its field next year manures, weeds and walls it: land yields more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: C1's first_settler_rights lets a founding lineage allot fields; household fields are heritable holdings of each household.

newNodes.name: Sealed stores
newNodes.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Tell Sabi Abyad (Syria): clay sealings on store jars and doors
newNodes.prereqRationale: stamp_seal: the seal impression is the control (~6,000 BCE). pottery_open_fired: sealed jars are the stores (far earlier).
newNodes.rationale: stamp_seal: the seal impression is the control (~6,000 BCE). pottery_open_fired: sealed jars are the stores (far earlier).
newNodes.desc: Store doors and jars are closed with clay pressed by an owner's seal; a broken sealing shows who took grain and when.
newNodes.effectRationale: Sealed jars and doors keep vermin and pilferers out of the grain: less is lost in store.
newNodes.distinctFrom: stamp_seal is the object; sealed stores are the custom of controlling and auditing store access with it.

newNodes.name: Village headship
newNodes.emerged: ~5,500 BCE Ubaid villages with a larger central house (inferred leadership); ethnographic analogy with village headmen
newNodes.prereqRationale: kin_council: the head is chosen from and by the household heads. cereal_cultivation: a permanent farming village needs a standing head (~11,500 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: kin_council: the head is chosen from and by the household heads. cereal_cultivation: a permanent farming village needs a standing head (~11,500 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: One household head is acknowledged as the village's head: he speaks for it to outsiders and calls the households to common work.
newNodes.effectRationale: The head calls work parties for ditches, walls and tracks: more path-building per worker.
newNodes.distinctFrom: kin_council decides by consensus; headship is a standing office in a settled village, not a regional chief (C1 chiefdom).

newNodes.name: Judges and court records
newNodes.emerged: ~2,100 BCE Ur III ditilla records of completed lawsuits; ~1,754 BCE judges in Hammurabi's laws
newNodes.prereqRationale: law_code: judges apply written law. appointed_officials: judges are officials named by the ruler (~2,600 BCE), earlier than the first case records (~2,100 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: law_code: judges apply written law. appointed_officials: judges are officials named by the ruler (~2,600 BCE), earlier than the first case records (~2,100 BCE).
newNodes.desc: Appointed judges hear cases, take witnesses' oaths and record the verdict on a tablet, so a decided case stays decided.
newNodes.effectRationale: Disputes end in a recorded verdict instead of self-help and brawls that stop work.
newNodes.distinctFrom: law_code is the text of the law; royal judges are the office that applies it and keeps records of verdicts.

newNodes.name: Ration lists
newNodes.emerged: ~3,000 BCE Uruk bevelled-rim bowls (inferred standard ration measure); ~2,050 BCE Ur III ration lists
newNodes.prereqRationale: taxation: rations are paid out of collected levies. temple_economy: the temple household (~3,200 BCE) is the first institution feeding dependents by fixed scale.
newNodes.rationale: taxation: rations are paid out of collected levies. temple_economy: the temple household (~3,200 BCE) is the first institution feeding dependents by fixed scale.
newNodes.desc: Dependents of temple and palace draw fixed monthly rations of barley, oil and wool by age and status, so a short year is shared out by rule.
newNodes.effectRationale: A scaled ration spreads a shortfall over everyone on the list, so fewer starve outright.
newNodes.distinctFrom: temple_economy is the institution; ration lists are the written scale by which its stores are paid out.

newNodes.name: Village and ward heads
newNodes.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Old Babylonian rabianum (village mayor) and city elders answering to the palace
newNodes.prereqRationale: village_headship: the community already has a head (~5,500 BCE). taxation: the state now holds that head responsible for its dues (~3,300 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: village_headship: the community already has a head (~5,500 BCE). taxation: the state now holds that head responsible for its dues (~3,300 BCE).
newNodes.desc: A head chosen in the village or city ward answers to the palace for its dues, labour levies and crimes, and speaks for it before officials.
newNodes.effectRationale: A local head who knows every household collects the levy more completely than an outsider.
newNodes.distinctFrom: elite_council is a council of great families at the centre; village heads link each local community to the state.

newNodes.name: Merchant colony courts
newNodes.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Old Assyrian karum at Kanesh deciding merchants' disputes
newNodes.prereqRationale: trade: a merchant colony abroad exists for long-distance trade (~3,500 BCE). law_code: its court applies the home city's written law.
newNodes.rationale: trade: a merchant colony abroad exists for long-distance trade (~3,500 BCE). law_code: its court applies the home city's written law.
newNodes.desc: Merchants abroad form a colony with its own court; disputes over debts and lost goods are settled on the spot under the home city's law.
newNodes.effectRationale: Disputes settled at the trading post, not sent home, mean fewer losses and delays on each caravan.
newNodes.distinctFrom: C3's commercial_law (A6) is a general merchant law; karum courts are an early colony court abroad.

newNodes.name: Published laws
newNodes.emerged: ~650 BCE Dreros law inscription (Crete); ~621 BCE Draco's laws displayed at Athens; ~450 BCE Gortyn code
newNodes.prereqRationale: law_code: the laws exist in writing. alphabet_vowels or abjad: an alphabet many citizens can read makes public display meaningful (Greek ~800 BCE, Phoenician ~1,050 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: law_code: the laws exist in writing. alphabet_vowels or abjad: an alphabet many citizens can read makes public display meaningful (Greek ~800 BCE, Phoenician ~1,050 BCE).
newNodes.desc: Laws are carved on stone and set up in public so any citizen who can read knows the rule and the penalty, and magistrates cannot invent them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Citizens can check a magistrate against the posted text: fewer grievances of arbitrary judgment.
newNodes.distinctFrom: law_code is law written by and for officials; published law is displayed for citizens to read.

newNodes.name: Royal storehouses
newNodes.emerged: ~509-493 BCE Persepolis Fortification tablets (Achaemenid stores and disbursements)
newNodes.prereqRationale: provincial_administration: stores are kept province by province (~2,300 BCE onward). royal_archives: every receipt and issue is filed (~2,400 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: provincial_administration: stores are kept province by province (~2,300 BCE onward). royal_archives: every receipt and issue is filed (~2,400 BCE).
newNodes.desc: Revenue in grain, wine and silver is held in sealed provincial storehouses and paid out only by written order, keeping years of reserves.
newNodes.effectRationale: A network of provincial stores holds several years of revenue in kind: granaries hold more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: storehouse_sealing controls one store; the treasury is a provincial network of stores run on written orders.

newNodes.name: Property classes
newNodes.emerged: ~594 BCE Solon's four property classes at Athens; ~550 BCE Servian classes at Rome (traditional)
newNodes.prereqRationale: citizen_assembly: the classes sort the members of an assembly (~700 BCE). census: classes are assigned by an assessment of wealth.
newNodes.rationale: citizen_assembly: the classes sort the members of an assembly (~700 BCE). census: classes are assigned by an assessment of wealth.
newNodes.desc: Citizens are ranked by assessed wealth instead of birth; a family that grows rich can climb into the classes that may hold office.
newNodes.effectRationale: Office by wealth rather than birth lets new families rise: faster promotion.
newNodes.distinctFrom: elite_council admits leading families by birth; property classes admit by assessed wealth.

newNodes.name: Extended citizenship
newNodes.emerged: ~338 BCE Roman grants of citizenship to Latin towns; 212 CE Constitutio Antoniniana
newNodes.prereqRationale: legal_code_roman: citizenship is a legal status with rights at law. citizen_assembly: it is membership of a citizen body (~700 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: legal_code_roman: citizenship is a legal status with rights at law. citizen_assembly: it is membership of a citizen body (~700 BCE).
newNodes.desc: Citizenship is granted to allies, freedmen and whole towns; new citizens may marry, trade, sue and settle anywhere under the common law.
newNodes.effectRationale: Citizens may settle and own property anywhere in the state: people move more freely.
newNodes.distinctFrom: citizen_assembly is the body of citizens; extended citizenship opens it to outsiders by law.

newNodes.name: Selection by lot
newNodes.emerged: ~487 BCE Athenian archons chosen by lot; ~462 BCE allotted jury panels
newNodes.prereqRationale: citizen_assembly: lots are drawn among citizens (~700 BCE). elected_magistracies: the lot replaced election for offices that already existed (~683 BCE).
newNodes.rationale: citizen_assembly: lots are drawn among citizens (~700 BCE). elected_magistracies: the lot replaced election for offices that already existed (~683 BCE).
newNodes.desc: Many offices are filled by drawing lots among eligible citizens, so no faction can buy or monopolize them and every citizen may serve.
newNodes.effectRationale: Factions cannot capture office by bribery or force, so their struggles cost less.
newNodes.distinctFrom: elected_magistracies choose by vote; sortition by lot.

newNodes.name: Household registers
newNodes.emerged: ~375 BCE Qin registration of households in groups of five; 2 CE Han population register
newNodes.prereqRationale: census: the register continues the count. provincial_administration: county and provincial officials keep it up to date (~2,300 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: census: the register continues the count. provincial_administration: county and provincial officials keep it up to date (~2,300 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: Every household is entered on a standing register kept by county officials, updated for births, deaths and moves; groups of five answer for each other's dues.
newNodes.effectRationale: A continuously updated register with mutual responsibility leaves few households off the tax rolls.
newNodes.distinctFrom: census is a periodic count; household registers are continuous and tie each household to duties.

newNodes.name: Courts of appeal
newNodes.emerged: ~800 CE Abbasid mazalim courts hearing complaints against officials; ~1,250 CE Parlement of Paris
newNodes.prereqRationale: legal_code_roman: appeal presupposes a systematic law that higher judges interpret. appointed_officials: appeal judges sit above appointed local judges.
newNodes.rationale: legal_code_roman: appeal presupposes a systematic law that higher judges interpret. appointed_officials: appeal judges sit above appointed local judges.
newNodes.desc: A higher court reviews the judgments of local judges and petitions against officials; a wrong verdict can be overturned without bribing the governor.
newNodes.effectRationale: A wrong verdict can be corrected: injustice by local judges stops turning into lasting grievance.
newNodes.distinctFrom: royal_judges decide cases at first instance; appellate courts review those decisions.

newNodes.name: Public notaries
newNodes.emerged: ~1,154 CE Genoese notarial cartulary (Giovanni Scriba); ~1,255 CE Rolandino's Summa artis notariae (Bologna)
newNodes.prereqRationale: legal_code_roman: notarial forms follow Roman law. commercial_law: the notary's main business is merchants' contracts (~800 CE onward).
newNodes.rationale: legal_code_roman: notarial forms follow Roman law. commercial_law: the notary's main business is merchants' contracts (~800 CE onward).
newNodes.desc: Licensed notaries draw up contracts, wills and sales in set forms and keep registers; a notarial deed is proof in any court.
newNodes.effectRationale: Contracts that prove themselves in court let merchants deal at a distance: price gaps close faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: witnessed_agreements rely on living witnesses; a notarial deed is a public record that proves itself.

newNodes.name: Law faculties
newNodes.emerged: ~1,088 CE teaching of the Digest at Bologna (Irnerius); ~1,155 CE Habita privilege for scholars
newNodes.prereqRationale: jurists: the faculties study and gloss the jurists' Digest (~100 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: jurists: the faculties study and gloss the jurists' Digest (~100 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: Masters lecture on the Roman Digest and train students in glossing and disputation; their graduates staff courts and chanceries across the realm.
newNodes.effectRationale: Law was the first faculty around which universities formed: a university with a law school matures faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: jurists are practitioners; law faculties are the organized teaching of law in universities.

newNodes.name: Exchequer audit
newNodes.emerged: ~1,110 CE English Exchequer; 1,130 CE first surviving pipe roll
newNodes.prereqRationale: taxation: the Exchequer audits the levy. abacus: accounts were cast on a chequered counting board (~300 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: taxation: the Exchequer audits the levy. abacus: accounts were cast on a chequered counting board (~300 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: Sheriffs account twice a year at a chequered counting table; sums owed and paid are written on rolls, and arrears follow the official until cleared.
newNodes.effectRationale: Audited collectors cannot pocket the difference: more of the levy reaches the treasury.
newNodes.distinctFrom: taxation declares the levy; the Exchequer audits each collector's account against it.

newNodes.name: Chancery enrolment
newNodes.emerged: ~1,199 CE English chancery rolls of outgoing letters and writs
newNodes.prereqRationale: appointed_officials: the chancery is a department of officials. royal_archives: enrolment extends archiving to every outgoing order (~2,400 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: appointed_officials: the chancery is a department of officials. royal_archives: enrolment extends archiving to every outgoing order (~2,400 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: Copies of every letter and writ sent out are entered on rolls, so the government knows what it has granted and ordered and can enforce it.
newNodes.effectRationale: Orders that are recorded can be checked and enforced far from the court: authority carries further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: royal_archives keep incoming records; chancery rolls copy every outgoing order.

newNodes.name: Village by-laws
newNodes.emerged: ~1,270 CE English manorial by-laws on harvest and grazing; ~1,300 CE Landsgemeinde of the Swiss forest cantons
newNodes.prereqRationale: kin_council: the village meeting of household heads. heavy_plough: open strip fields worked in common need common rules (~500 CE onward).
newNodes.rationale: kin_council: the village meeting of household heads. heavy_plough: open strip fields worked in common need common rules (~500 CE onward).
newNodes.desc: The village meeting sets the dates of ploughing, harvest and gleaning and the number of beasts on the common, and fines those who break the rules.
newNodes.effectRationale: Coordinated rotation, fallow grazing and stinted commons keep the open fields fertile.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_charter governs towns; village by-laws govern open-field farming by the village meeting.

newNodes.name: Intendants
newNodes.emerged: ~1,635 CE French intendants made permanent under Richelieu
newNodes.prereqRationale: provincial_administration: intendants supervise existing provinces. royal_post: they report by regular post to the council (~550 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: provincial_administration: intendants supervise existing provinces. royal_post: they report by regular post to the council (~550 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: Royal commissioners, removable at will and paid by the crown, oversee justice, police and finance in each province and report by post to the council.
newNodes.effectRationale: Removable commissioners replace venal officers who owned their posts: the centre's orders are carried out in distant provinces.
newNodes.distinctFrom: provincial_administration places governors; intendants are revocable commissioners checking them and the venal officers.

newNodes.name: Bankruptcy law
newNodes.emerged: ~1,542 CE English Statute of Bankrupts; 1,705 CE discharge of honest bankrupts (England)
newNodes.prereqRationale: commercial_law: the law of merchants' debts (~800 CE onward). legal_code_roman: collective proceedings rest on systematic law.
newNodes.rationale: commercial_law: the law of merchants' debts (~800 CE onward). legal_code_roman: collective proceedings rest on systematic law.
newNodes.desc: When a trader fails, his goods are gathered and shared among creditors by rule, and an honest debtor can be discharged and trade again.
newNodes.effectRationale: Creditors who know what they will recover lend to traders more readily: goods move toward better prices faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: commercial_law covers contracts between solvent merchants; bankruptcy law governs what happens when one fails.

newNodes.name: Administrative courts
newNodes.emerged: 1,799 CE French Conseil d'Etat; 1,872 CE its independent jurisdiction
newNodes.prereqRationale: separation_of_powers: a court separate from the administration (1748 onward). appointed_officials: the officials whose acts it reviews.
newNodes.rationale: separation_of_powers: a court separate from the administration (1748 onward). appointed_officials: the officials whose acts it reviews.
newNodes.desc: Citizens can sue the administration before specialist judges; officials who exceed their powers see their acts annulled, so every province is run by the same rules.
newNodes.effectRationale: Officials held to legal rules everywhere: the centre's rules apply uniformly far from the capital.
newNodes.distinctFrom: judicial_review tests laws against the constitution; administrative courts test officials' acts against the law.

newNodes.name: Penitentiaries
newNodes.emerged: 1,790 CE Walnut Street Jail (Philadelphia); 1,842 CE Pentonville prison (London)
newNodes.prereqRationale: civil_police: offenders are arrested by a standing force (1667 onward). enlightenment: Beccaria's and Howard's reform arguments (1687 onward).
newNodes.rationale: civil_police: offenders are arrested by a standing force (1667 onward). enlightenment: Beccaria's and Howard's reform arguments (1687 onward).
newNodes.desc: Prison terms graded by offence replace branding, flogging and the gallows for most crimes; convicts are held, worked and released rather than maimed or killed.
newNodes.effectRationale: Public executions and floggings drew riotous crowds; graded imprisonment removes the spectacle and the disorder.
newNodes.distinctFrom: civil_police arrests offenders; penitentiaries decide what is done with them after conviction.

newNodes.name: Married women's property
newNodes.emerged: 1,839 CE Mississippi Married Women's Property Act; 1,882 CE English Married Women's Property Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: family_law: reforms the law of marriage and estates. classical_liberalism: equal legal personality argued from 1776 onward (Mill).
newNodes.rationale: family_law: reforms the law of marriage and estates. classical_liberalism: equal legal personality argued from 1776 onward (Mill).
newNodes.desc: A wife keeps her own earnings, property and inheritance and may contract and sue in her own name, so women can run shops and enter trades.
newNodes.effectRationale: Women who own what they earn can keep a shop or trade: larger specialist classes become possible.
newNodes.distinctFrom: family_law fixes marriage and inheritance; this act gives wives separate legal personality in property.

newNodes.name: Trademark law
newNodes.emerged: 1,857 CE French trademark law; 1,875 CE UK Trade Marks Registration Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: patent: trademarks are registered industrial property like patents. railway: national markets carried branded goods far from their maker (1830 onward).
newNodes.rationale: patent: trademarks are registered industrial property like patents. railway: national markets carried branded goods far from their maker (1830 onward).
newNodes.desc: Makers register their marks and copying one is a wrong, so buyers far away can trust a branded sack of flour or tin of tea.
newNodes.effectRationale: Goods whose quality is known by their mark sell at a distance without inspection: stocks reach markets faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: patent protects an invention; a trademark protects a maker's name on goods.

newNodes.name: Prefects
newNodes.emerged: 1,800 CE French prefects (law of 28 Pluviose year VIII)
newNodes.prereqRationale: provincial_intendants: the prefect is the intendant's successor (1635). official_statistics: prefects compiled the departmental statistics of 1801 (1749 onward).
newNodes.rationale: provincial_intendants: the prefect is the intendant's successor (1635). official_statistics: prefects compiled the departmental statistics of 1801 (1749 onward).
newNodes.desc: Each uniform department is run by a prefect appointed by and answering to the interior ministry, applying the same laws, levies and conscription everywhere.
newNodes.effectRationale: One chain of command over uniform departments: authority reaches the whole country. 0.05: the template of the modern centralized state.
newNodes.distinctFrom: provincial_intendants supervised historic provinces with mixed privileges; prefects run uniform departments under one ministry.

newNodes.name: Civil registration
newNodes.emerged: 1,792 CE French etat civil; 1,837 CE General Register Office (England and Wales)
newNodes.prereqRationale: official_statistics: registration feeds the vital tables (1749 onward). secular_state: registers pass from the parish clergy to the state (1791 onward).
newNodes.rationale: official_statistics: registration feeds the vital tables (1749 onward). secular_state: registers pass from the parish clergy to the state (1791 onward).
newNodes.desc: Every birth, marriage and death is recorded by a public registrar; each person has a legal identity, and the state sees where infants are dying.
newNodes.effectRationale: Registered births let relief officers find orphans and foundlings when food is short: children are better protected.
newNodes.distinctFrom: official_statistics publishes tables; civil registration is the record of each person from which they are drawn.

newNodes.name: Abolition of internal tolls
newNodes.emerged: 1,790 CE abolition of internal customs in France; 1,818 CE Prussian customs law
newNodes.prereqRationale: customs_tolls: the tolls being abolished. provincial_administration: a central administration able to replace provincial duties with one frontier tariff.
newNodes.rationale: customs_tolls: the tolls being abolished. provincial_administration: a central administration able to replace provincial duties with one frontier tariff.
newNodes.desc: Tolls at provincial borders, rivers and town gates are abolished; duties are collected once, at the national frontier, by one customs service.
newNodes.effectRationale: Goods cross a country without paying at every river and gate: cheaper haulage.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customs_tolls levy duties at internal gates; this replaces them with one frontier tariff. C3's customs_union joins several states' tariffs.

newNodes.name: Elected town councils
newNodes.emerged: 1,808 CE Prussian Stadteordnung; 1,835 CE Municipal Corporations Act (England)
newNodes.prereqRationale: municipal_charter: the town already governs itself (~90 CE onward). representative_assembly: the council is elected by ratepayers (1188 onward).
newNodes.rationale: municipal_charter: the town already governs itself (~90 CE onward). representative_assembly: the council is elected by ratepayers (1188 onward).
newNodes.desc: Ratepayers elect a town council with a budget of its own; it paves, lights and drains streets and maintains the roads of its district.
newNodes.effectRationale: Rate-funded councils with their own surveyors build and keep local roads more cheaply.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_charter grants self-government to an oligarchy; elected councils answer to all ratepayers and run public works.

newNodes.name: Elected rural councils
newNodes.emerged: 1,864 CE Russian zemstvo reform; 1,888 CE English county councils
newNodes.prereqRationale: municipal_corporations: elected councils on the town model (1808). abolition: the zemstvo was created after the emancipation of the serfs (1861) to give the countryside its own government.
newNodes.rationale: municipal_corporations: elected councils on the town model (1808). abolition: the zemstvo was created after the emancipation of the serfs (1861) to give the countryside its own government.
newNodes.desc: Elected district councils of landowners, townsmen and peasants run rural schools, clinics, roads and grain reserves for relief in bad years.
newNodes.effectRationale: Zemstvo grain reserves and relief committees (1891-92) make stored food reach the hungry.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_corporations govern towns; zemstvos govern the countryside.

newNodes.name: Patent Cooperation Treaty
newNodes.emerged: 1,970 CE Patent Cooperation Treaty; 1,994 CE TRIPS agreement
newNodes.prereqRationale: patent: national patent systems. international_organizations: the treaty is administered by an international bureau (1865 onward).
newNodes.rationale: patent: national patent systems. international_organizations: the treaty is administered by an international bureau (1865 onward).
newNodes.desc: One international application and search covers many countries: inventors file once, and laboratories can see what is already claimed anywhere.
newNodes.effectRationale: Worldwide prior-art search keeps research teams from repeating work already patented elsewhere.
newNodes.distinctFrom: patent is a national grant; this is one international filing and search for all members.

newNodes.name: Land to the tiller
newNodes.emerged: 1,917 CE Mexican constitution, Article 27 (ejidos); 1,946 CE Japanese land reform; 1,953 CE Taiwan
newNodes.prereqRationale: land_registry: title must be recorded to be transferred. mass_suffrage: enfranchised peasants made redistribution a political demand (1820 onward).
newNodes.rationale: land_registry: title must be recorded to be transferred. mass_suffrage: enfranchised peasants made redistribution a political demand (1820 onward).
newNodes.desc: The state buys out absentee landlords and sells their land in small plots to the tenants who farm it; owner-farmers invest in their own fields.
newNodes.effectRationale: Owner-cultivators keep the whole crop and work harder and better (Japan, Korea, Taiwan after 1946). 0.04: a landmark reform.
newNodes.distinctFrom: household_land_tenure recognizes existing holdings; land reform transfers land from landlords to tenants.

newNodes.name: Tenancy protection
newNodes.emerged: 1,881 CE Irish Land Act (fair rent and fixity of tenure, a forerunner); 1,978 CE Operation Barga in West Bengal
newNodes.prereqRationale: land_registry: tenancies are registered. civil_code: the law of leases is codified and courts can enforce fixed terms (1804 onward).
newNodes.rationale: land_registry: tenancies are registered. civil_code: the law of leases is codified and courts can enforce fixed terms (1804 onward).
newNodes.desc: Sharecroppers are registered and cannot be evicted while they pay a fixed share; secure tenants manure, drain and double-crop the land.
newNodes.effectRationale: Secure tenants invest in the land (Banerjee, Gertler and Ghatak on Operation Barga): land yields more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: land_reform transfers ownership; tenancy protection leaves ownership but secures the tenant.

newNodes.name: International arbitration
newNodes.emerged: 1,923 CE ICC Court of Arbitration (Paris); 1,958 CE New York Convention
newNodes.prereqRationale: commercial_law: merchants' own law of contract. international_organizations: the convention binds many states (1865 onward).
newNodes.rationale: commercial_law: merchants' own law of contract. international_organizations: the convention binds many states (1865 onward).
newNodes.desc: Traders in different countries choose private arbitrators whose awards courts everywhere enforce, so a cross-border deal no longer hangs on a foreign judge.
newNodes.effectRationale: Enforceable awards cut the risk premium on long-distance contracts: cheaper trade.
newNodes.distinctFrom: karum_courts settled disputes within one merchant colony; arbitration awards are enforceable across states.

newNodes.name: Refugee protection
newNodes.emerged: 1,922 CE Nansen passport; 1,951 CE Refugee Convention
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the League's High Commissioner issued the first papers (1865 onward). law_of_nations: duties between states toward foreigners (1625).
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the League's High Commissioner issued the first papers (1865 onward). law_of_nations: duties between states toward foreigners (1625).
newNodes.desc: People fleeing persecution receive travel papers and may not be sent back to danger; states share the task of receiving them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Papers and a duty not to return refugees let them cross several borders to safety: migrants travel further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: human_rights declares rights in general; refugee law gives a specific status and travel papers to the displaced.

newNodes.name: Equal pay law
newNodes.emerged: 1,951 CE ILO Equal Remuneration Convention; 1,963 CE US Equal Pay Act; 1,970 CE UK Equal Pay Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: womens_suffrage: women voters pressed the law (1893 onward). labour_unions: pay is set by bargaining that the law now constrains (1824 onward).
newNodes.rationale: womens_suffrage: women voters pressed the law (1893 onward). labour_unions: pay is set by bargaining that the law now constrains (1824 onward).
newNodes.desc: Employers must pay women the same as men for the same work, so more women train for and stay in skilled and professional jobs.
newNodes.effectRationale: Equal pay makes skilled work worth training for: larger specialist classes become possible.
newNodes.distinctFrom: married_womens_property gave wives control of earnings; equal pay governs what employers must pay.

newNodes.name: Consumer protection
newNodes.emerged: 1,938 CE US Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act; 1,973 CE UK Fair Trading Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: civil_code: contract law on which buyers' rights are built (1804). antitrust: consumer law grew out of competition law (1890 onward).
newNodes.rationale: civil_code: contract law on which buyers' rights are built (1804). antitrust: consumer law grew out of competition law (1890 onward).
newNodes.desc: Labels must state contents, weights must be true and dangerous goods can be recalled, so buyers trust goods from distant makers.
newNodes.effectRationale: Buyers who trust distant sellers widen markets: price gaps close faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: trademark_law protects the seller's mark; consumer protection protects the buyer against the seller.

newNodes.name: Legal aid
newNodes.emerged: 1,949 CE Legal Aid and Advice Act (England); 1,963 CE Gideon v. Wainwright (right to counsel)
newNodes.prereqRationale: bill_of_rights: a right to a fair trial (1215 onward). jurists: a legal profession whose services the state now pays for (~100 BCE onward).
newNodes.rationale: bill_of_rights: a right to a fair trial (1215 onward). jurists: a legal profession whose services the state now pays for (~100 BCE onward).
newNodes.desc: The state pays for a lawyer for those who cannot afford one, in criminal trials and in disputes over wages, housing and family.
newNodes.effectRationale: Poor households can defend their wages, tenancies and liberty in court instead of losing them: fewer are pushed down and more rise.
newNodes.distinctFrom: jurists serve those who can pay; legal aid extends counsel to everyone.

newNodes.name: Tax withholding
newNodes.emerged: 1,943 CE US Current Tax Payment Act; 1,944 CE PAYE (Britain)
newNodes.prereqRationale: income_tax: the tax being withheld (1799). punched_card_tabulation: payroll machines compute each deduction (1889 onward).
newNodes.rationale: income_tax: the tax being withheld (1799). punched_card_tabulation: payroll machines compute each deduction (1889 onward).
newNodes.desc: Employers deduct income tax from every wage packet and pay it to the state; wage earners pay as they earn and evasion falls.
newNodes.effectRationale: Tax taken at source cannot be evaded or defaulted on: the levy extracts far more. 0.05: the basis of the mass income tax.
newNodes.distinctFrom: income_tax assesses declared incomes; withholding collects it at the payroll.

newNodes.name: Value-added tax
newNodes.emerged: 1,954 CE France (Maurice Laure); 1,967 CE Brazil and Denmark
newNodes.prereqRationale: income_tax: a mature tax administration. double_entry: the credit-invoice method needs firms' accounts of sales and purchases (~1,300 CE onward).
newNodes.rationale: income_tax: a mature tax administration. double_entry: the credit-invoice method needs firms' accounts of sales and purchases (~1,300 CE onward).
newNodes.desc: Each firm pays tax on the value it adds and deducts the tax paid on its inputs; invoices check one another, and exports leave untaxed.
newNodes.effectRationale: Self-checking invoices raise revenue; refunds on inputs and zero-rated exports remove cascading tax from goods that travel.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customs_tolls tax goods at gates; VAT taxes value added at each stage with credit for tax already paid.

newNodes.name: Executive budget
newNodes.emerged: 1,921 CE US Budget and Accounting Act (Bureau of the Budget, General Accounting Office)
newNodes.prereqRationale: income_tax: the revenue base the budget plans (1799). ministerial_responsibility: the cabinet answers to the chamber for one budget (1782 onward).
newNodes.rationale: income_tax: the revenue base the budget plans (1799). ministerial_responsibility: the cabinet answers to the chamber for one budget (1782 onward).
newNodes.desc: A central budget office prepares one plan of revenue and spending for every department and audits it afterwards, so distant agencies spend as planned.
newNodes.effectRationale: Every agency's spending is planned and audited from the centre: authority reaches its far offices.
newNodes.distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks collectors after the fact; the executive budget plans all spending before it happens.

newNodes.name: Sample surveys
newNodes.emerged: 1,937 CE Mahalanobis crop surveys of Bengal jute; 1,940 CE US monthly labour-force sample
newNodes.prereqRationale: official_statistics: the statistical office runs the surveys (1749 onward). probability_statistics: random sampling and error estimation (1654 onward).
newNodes.rationale: official_statistics: the statistical office runs the surveys (1749 onward). probability_statistics: random sampling and error estimation (1654 onward).
newNodes.desc: Statisticians measure a random sample of fields and households instead of all, giving crop and employment estimates within weeks, in time to move stocks.
newNodes.effectRationale: Early crop estimates tell traders and stores where to send grain before prices spike: stocks reach markets faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: official_statistics counts everyone; sample surveys estimate quickly from a random part.

newNodes.name: Fiscal equalization
newNodes.emerged: 1,933 CE Commonwealth Grants Commission (Australia); 1,957 CE Canadian equalization payments
newNodes.prereqRationale: income_tax: central revenue to redistribute (1799). federal_republic: transfers between the federation and its states (1787).
newNodes.rationale: income_tax: central revenue to redistribute (1799). federal_republic: transfers between the federation and its states (1787).
newNodes.desc: The central treasury transfers revenue to poorer or stricken regions by formula, so provinces can keep services and relief going after a bad year.
newNodes.effectRationale: Regions hit by a bad year keep their relief and services funded: households absorb the shortfall.
newNodes.distinctFrom: income_tax raises revenue; equalization moves it to regions that need it.

newNodes.name: Customs modernization
newNodes.emerged: ~1,981 CE ASYCUDA computerized customs; 1,988 CE Harmonized System of tariff nomenclature
newNodes.prereqRationale: multilateral_trade_rules: common tariff rules and valuation (1947). computer: declarations processed electronically (1948 onward).
newNodes.rationale: multilateral_trade_rules: common tariff rules and valuation (1947). computer: declarations processed electronically (1948 onward).
newNodes.desc: Goods are classified by one world nomenclature and declared electronically; most cargo clears in hours, with checks targeted by risk.
newNodes.effectRationale: Hours instead of days at the border: cheaper haulage.
newNodes.distinctFrom: internal_toll_abolition removes internal duties; customs modernization speeds the frontier itself.

newNodes.name: Competitive procurement
newNodes.emerged: 1,979 CE GATT Government Procurement Code; 1,994 CE WTO Agreement on Government Procurement
newNodes.prereqRationale: merit_civil_service: impartial officials run the tender (1854). multilateral_trade_rules: the procurement codes are part of the trade rules (1947).
newNodes.rationale: merit_civil_service: impartial officials run the tender (1854). multilateral_trade_rules: the procurement codes are part of the trade rules (1947).
newNodes.desc: Public works are let by open, advertised tender under published rules, and contracts go to the lowest compliant bid rather than to friends of officials.
newNodes.effectRationale: Competitive tenders cut the price of roads and works the state pays for.
newNodes.distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks what was spent; procurement governs how contracts are awarded.

newNodes.name: Agricultural extension
newNodes.emerged: 1,914 CE Smith-Lever Act (US Cooperative Extension Service)
newNodes.prereqRationale: research_university: land-grant colleges train the agents (1810 onward). agricultural_chemistry: the fertiliser and soil science they teach (1813 onward).
newNodes.rationale: research_university: land-grant colleges train the agents (1810 onward). agricultural_chemistry: the fertiliser and soil science they teach (1813 onward).
newNodes.desc: Public agents trained at agricultural colleges visit farms, run demonstration plots and teach new seed, fertiliser and methods to working farmers.
newNodes.effectRationale: Demonstrated methods spread from college to farm within a season: each farmer produces more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: agricultural_chemistry is the science; extension is the public service that carries it to farmers.

newNodes.name: Disaster management
newNodes.emerged: 1,950 CE US Federal Civil Defense Administration; 1,979 CE FEMA; 2,005 CE India's National Disaster Management Authority
newNodes.prereqRationale: official_statistics: needs are assessed from population data (1749 onward). radio_broadcasting: warnings reach everyone at once (1920 onward).
newNodes.rationale: official_statistics: needs are assessed from population data (1749 onward). radio_broadcasting: warnings reach everyone at once (1920 onward).
newNodes.desc: A standing agency plans for flood, drought and earthquake, stocks relief, broadcasts warnings and moves food and shelter to the stricken within days.
newNodes.effectRationale: Relief planned and stocked in advance reaches the stricken before hunger kills: fewer famine deaths.
newNodes.distinctFrom: zemstvo_councils kept local grain reserves; a disaster agency plans and moves relief nationally.

newNodes.name: Freedom of information
newNodes.emerged: 1,951 CE Finnish Act on the Publicity of Official Documents; 1,966 CE US Freedom of Information Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: press_freedom: journalists use the files (1766 onward). merit_civil_service: a records-keeping bureaucracy bound by rules (1854).
newNodes.rationale: press_freedom: journalists use the files (1766 onward). merit_civil_service: a records-keeping bureaucracy bound by rules (1854).
newNodes.desc: Any citizen may request government files and must receive them unless a stated exemption applies, so abuses come to light and are corrected.
newNodes.effectRationale: Exposed abuses are corrected instead of resented in silence.
newNodes.distinctFrom: C5's press_freedom lets publishers print; freedom of information compels the state to open its files.

newNodes.name: Digital government
newNodes.emerged: ~2,000 CE online tax filing; ~2,001 CE Estonia's X-Road data exchange
newNodes.prereqRationale: internet: services delivered online (1983 onward). merit_civil_service: the bureaucracy being digitized (1854).
newNodes.rationale: internet: services delivered online (1983 onward). merit_civil_service: the bureaucracy being digitized (1854).
newNodes.desc: Citizens file taxes, register businesses and claim benefits online; agencies share data through secure links, so remote districts are served as well as the capital.
newNodes.effectRationale: Distance from the capital stops mattering for a service delivered online: administrative reach extends further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: chancery_rolls and executive_budget are paper records; digital government delivers the services themselves online.

newNodes.name: Digital identity
newNodes.emerged: ~2,002 CE Estonian electronic ID card; 2,009 CE India's Aadhaar
newNodes.prereqRationale: e_government: the services the ID unlocks (~2,000 CE). civil_registration: the identity records it is built on (1792).
newNodes.rationale: e_government: the services the ID unlocks (~2,000 CE). civil_registration: the identity records it is built on (1792).
newNodes.desc: Every resident has a unique, verifiable digital identity; entitlements such as rations and pensions can be drawn anywhere, so workers can move without losing them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Portable entitlements (India's One Nation One Ration Card) remove a reason not to move.
newNodes.distinctFrom: civil_registration records identity on paper locally; digital identity verifies it anywhere online.

newNodes.name: Road traffic law
newNodes.emerged: 1,926 CE International Convention relative to Motor Traffic (Paris); 1,968 CE Vienna Convention on Road Traffic
newNodes.prereqRationale: automobile_mass: mass motor traffic to regulate (1913). civil_police: traffic police enforce the rules (1667 onward).
newNodes.rationale: automobile_mass: mass motor traffic to regulate (1913). civil_police: traffic police enforce the rules (1667 onward).
newNodes.desc: Licensed drivers, registered vehicles, speed limits, uniform signs and right-of-way rules let heavy motor traffic flow safely between towns.
newNodes.effectRationale: Uniform rules and signs keep mixed traffic moving: faster overland travel.
newNodes.distinctFrom: C3's zoning plans land use; traffic law governs movement on the roads.

newNodes.name: Anti-corruption commission
newNodes.emerged: 1,952 CE Singapore Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau; 1,974 CE Hong Kong ICAC
newNodes.prereqRationale: merit_civil_service: a service with rules to enforce (1854). civil_police: the commission's investigators and powers of arrest come from police practice (1667 onward).
newNodes.rationale: merit_civil_service: a service with rules to enforce (1854). civil_police: the commission's investigators and powers of arrest come from police practice (1667 onward).
newNodes.desc: An independent commission investigates officials' bribes and kickbacks with power to arrest, so revenue stops leaking between taxpayer and treasury.
newNodes.effectRationale: Less leakage in collection: taxes extract more of what is owed.
newNodes.distinctFrom: exchequer_audit checks accounts; an anti-corruption commission investigates and prosecutes officials.

newNodes.name: Administrative procedure law
newNodes.emerged: 1,946 CE US Administrative Procedure Act; 1,976 CE German Administrative Procedure Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: administrative_courts: courts review agency decisions (1799). merit_civil_service: the agencies bound by the procedure (1854).
newNodes.rationale: administrative_courts: courts review agency decisions (1799). merit_civil_service: the agencies bound by the procedure (1854).
newNodes.desc: Agencies must publish proposed rules, hear comments and give reasons for decisions, which courts can review; those affected are heard before, not after.
newNodes.effectRationale: People heard before a rule is made protest less after it: unrest costs less output.
newNodes.distinctFrom: administrative_courts annul unlawful acts afterwards; administrative procedure governs how decisions are made.

newNodes.name: Proportional representation
newNodes.emerged: 1,899 CE Belgium; 1,918-1,920 CE adopted across much of continental Europe
newNodes.prereqRationale: mass_suffrage: a mass electorate (1820 onward). mass_political_party: seats are allotted to party lists (1830 onward).
newNodes.rationale: mass_suffrage: a mass electorate (1820 onward). mass_political_party: seats are allotted to party lists (1830 onward).
newNodes.desc: Seats are shared among parties in proportion to their votes, so minorities and new movements win a voice in the chamber instead of the street.
newNodes.effectRationale: Minorities represented in the chamber accumulate less grievance against it.
newNodes.distinctFrom: mass_suffrage gives everyone a vote; proportional representation makes each vote count toward seats.

newNodes.name: Regional self-government
newNodes.emerged: 1,947 CE Italian constitution's regions; 1,978 CE Spanish autonomous communities; 1,999 CE UK devolution
newNodes.prereqRationale: provincial_administration: the regions already exist as administrative units. mass_suffrage: their governments are now elected (1820 onward).
newNodes.rationale: provincial_administration: the regions already exist as administrative units. mass_suffrage: their governments are now elected (1820 onward).
newNodes.desc: Elected regional assemblies and governments take over schools, health and roads within a region, extending effective government to its far corners.
newNodes.effectRationale: Regional governments administer what the capital could not reach: administrative reach extends.
newNodes.distinctFrom: provincial_administration appoints governors from the centre; devolution elects regional governments.

newNodes.name: Reserved seats
newNodes.emerged: 1,950 CE Indian constitution's reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes; 1,993 CE one third of village council seats reserved for women (India)
newNodes.prereqRationale: mass_suffrage: excluded groups vote. written_constitution: the reservation is a constitutional guarantee (1653 onward).
newNodes.rationale: mass_suffrage: excluded groups vote. written_constitution: the reservation is a constitutional guarantee (1653 onward).
newNodes.desc: A share of seats and council headships is set aside for excluded castes, tribes or women; their members gain office, patronage and a route upward.
newNodes.effectRationale: Reserved office raises members of excluded groups into public positions (Pande 2003): faster promotion.
newNodes.distinctFrom: C1's power_sharing divides offices among communities; reserved seats guarantee places for disadvantaged groups within any party system.

newNodes.name: Participatory budgeting
newNodes.emerged: 1,989 CE Porto Alegre
newNodes.prereqRationale: municipal_corporations: an elected city government with an investment budget (1808). mass_suffrage: every resident takes part (1820 onward).
newNodes.rationale: municipal_corporations: an elected city government with an investment budget (1808). mass_suffrage: every resident takes part (1820 onward).
newNodes.desc: Neighbourhood assemblies vote each year on which streets, drains and clinics the city's investment budget will build, and monitor the works.
newNodes.effectRationale: Works chosen and watched by the neighbourhood are built with less waste.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_corporations decide budgets in council; participatory budgeting gives the decision to neighbourhood assemblies.

newNodes.name: Elected village councils
newNodes.emerged: 1,959 CE panchayati raj in Rajasthan; 1,992 CE India's 73rd Amendment
newNodes.prereqRationale: zemstvo_councils: elected rural government (1864). mass_suffrage: every villager votes (1820 onward).
newNodes.rationale: zemstvo_councils: elected rural government (1864). mass_suffrage: every villager votes (1820 onward).
newNodes.desc: Every village elects a council with its own funds and duties; it runs public works and relief schemes and decides who needs help when harvests fail.
newNodes.effectRationale: Relief allocated by people who know each household reaches those in need: households absorb shortfalls.
newNodes.distinctFrom: zemstvo_councils govern a district; elected village councils govern each village.

newNodes.name: Metropolitan government
newNodes.emerged: 1,954 CE Metropolitan Toronto; 1,965 CE Greater London Council
newNodes.prereqRationale: municipal_corporations: the town councils being federated (1808). automobile_mass: suburbs spread beyond city limits by car (1913).
newNodes.rationale: municipal_corporations: the town councils being federated (1808). automobile_mass: suburbs spread beyond city limits by car (1913).
newNodes.desc: One authority plans transport, water and land use for a city and its suburbs together, so the whole commuting region works as one.
newNodes.effectRationale: A city governed with its suburbs draws on a wider region.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_corporations govern within city limits; metropolitan government spans the whole urban region.

newLanes.name: public-administration
newLanes.scope: The administrative state's service and oversight agencies (A9 onward): extension services, disaster management, information access, digital government and identity, traffic regulation, administrative procedure and anti-corruption. Split from administration-fiscal, which keeps levies, budgets, registers, statistics and revenue institutions.

findings: Dependency changes proposed: 2, no Age moves. census replaces stamp_seal with appointed_officials (a count is an act of officials; stamp_seal stays in the closure through taxation). merit_civil_service replaces appointed_officials with civil_service_examinations (Northcote-Trevelyan took the Chinese examination model via Haileybury; the A6 node otherwise has a single regime dependent). Every other edge is kept; Age and tree crossings were not treated as reasons.

Effects: all 41 audited nodes carry an effect. Only legal_code_roman (inst.university) and taxation (order.tax_edict) have live unlocks today; the other 39 were knowledge-only (institutions or M8 policy/regime modules) and now carry operand effects. Within every lane+Age no two nodes share the same single operand.

New lane declared: public-administration (8 A9 nodes: extension, disaster management, freedom of information, digital government and identity, traffic law, anti-corruption, administrative procedure). Without it the A9 fiscal lane would need ~15 distinct operands for a single domain.

Operand pressure: with T1-T8 and C1 already written, society.grievanceRelief sums to 1.05 against cap 0.6 (C2 adds 0.33 over 13 nodes at 0.02-0.04), society.unrestOutputDrag 0.83 against 0.6 (C2 0.23), research.civicsPointsCoefficient 0.33 against 0.3 (C2 only 0.02). governance.taxExtractionResponseMax is at 1.20 of 1.5 (C2 0.42) and will pass the cap once C3 adds fiscal nodes. The integrator should rescale the society operands per tree or raise their caps; C2 routed most administrative nodes to governance.authorityDecayCostUnits (1.82 of 3.0) to leave headroom.

Missing emerged dates on four runtime civics (law_code, legal_code_roman, census, patent); suggested texts are in their audit rationales. Date-Age mismatches noted, not acted on: elite_council (A3) cites only ~700 BCE and later; legal_code_roman (A4) is evidenced by the Twelve Tables (~450 BCE) and later.

Leaves bridged by new nodes: family_law, jurists, patent, civil_police, civil_code, income_tax, merit_civil_service. Deliberate leaves kept: corvee_labour, tax_farming, jury_courts, state_monopolies, common_law, copyright, judicial_review, referendum, secret_ballot, womens_suffrage (equal_pay_law hangs on it), human_rights, international_tribunals.

Dating notes on new nodes: blood_compensation and witnessed_agreements are A2 pre-literate practices whose only era-marked dates are their first written attestations (~2,100 and ~2,600 BCE). proportional_representation (1899 Belgium) and tenancy_protection (1881 Irish forerunner) carry late-A8 origins but sit in A9, where the modern forms spread.

Coordination: C1 already authored constitutional_court and electoral_commission, so C2 did not. Possible topic overlap with C3 (land_reform, tenancy_protection, consumer_protection, bankruptcy_law, trademark_law, equal_pay_law, internal_toll_abolition vs customs_union, disaster_management) and C5 (freedom_of_information vs press_freedom); the integrator should dedupe by topic as well as id.

Pacing: A9 civics grows by 29 here (plus C1's A9 nodes), so the per-node A9 civic cost must fall under the section 5 scale; new A9 magnitudes are 7.0-8.0 (median ~16,700 before scaling) against an existing A9 median of 28,130. census (2.0x the A4 median) and civil_service_examinations (1.68x the A6 median) are the dearest audited nodes for their Ages. mass_suffrage's desc says 'by secret ballot', duplicating secret_ballot; suggest dropping the phrase.
